name: Onboard a new client and transition its assets
summary: This process takes a public body that has chosen the asset manager from that decision to having its assets moved, its accounts and systems set up and a day-one transition report in its hands. The relationship manager runs a cross-functional project: legal negotiates the investment management agreement, compliance checks KYC and codes the client's restrictions, operations opens custody and unitholder accounts, portfolio construction maps the client's policy to pools, and manager research plans how legacy mandates are kept, sold or moved in kind. Most of the elapsed time is waiting on outside parties: the client's lawyers and board calendar, a government regulation for new types of client, the custodian's account opening and the old custodian's deliveries. It happens about once a year, so few staff have done it before and the steps are coordinated by checklist and email.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Covers a new client portfolio after selection: IMA, KYC, eligibility, account and system set-up, transfer of legacy assets and the transition report. The proposal stage and the later full asset mix review are separate processes. In the period two clients joined (the judges' plan in March 2020, mostly cash, and WISE Trust); four more were selected in December 2023.

trigger: A public body confirms it has selected the asset manager (after a proposal, a direct approach or a government decision) and the onboarding project is opened.
end_state: The IMA is signed, the client is a member, accounts and systems are live, legacy assets have been received and reconciled and placed in pools or segregated holdings, and the client has a transition report with day-one positions, values and costs; or the client withdraws.

volume.seasonality: Lumpy: none in most years, then several at once when a group of public bodies selects the manager (four were selected together in December 2023). Transfers are usually timed for a month end.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file: two clients joined in 2020 (judges' plan and WISE Trust), none in 2021 or 2022 per the organisation file, four selected in 2023; about one a year on average.

steps.name: Open the onboarding project
steps.description: After the public body confirms it has chosen the model manager, the relationship manager opens the client record in the CRM, names the cross-functional onboarding team (legal, compliance, portfolio construction, operations, finance, data) and drafts a project plan with the target transfer date. A kick-off call with the client's staff agrees the document list, the interim investment approach and the governance dates that will set the timeline.
inputs: client selection letter or accepted proposal

error.defect_description: Project plan misses a client governance date or a legacy holding type, discovered later.

evidence.note: Selection precedes onboarding, which waits on contracts and regulation; multi-party project planning described in the transition case study. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Request KYC and onboarding documents
steps.description: The relationship manager sends the client a request list: governing statute or constating documents, board resolution and authorised signers with specimen signatures, accredited investor certificate, current investment policy or interim restrictions, latest custodian and manager statements, the list of legacy mandates and private fund interests, and contacts at the current custodian.

error.defect_description: Request list omits a document the custodian later requires.

evidence.note: KYC policy and accredited investor certification required by the OSC decision; custodian document types from the State Street roundtable. Touch time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Client gathers and returns documents
steps.description: The client's finance and legal staff assemble the documents, obtain board extracts and signatures and ask their current custodian and managers for holdings files. They upload the package to the shared document site or email it in parts.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Wait of one to four weeks is an author estimate for a public body that must collect board extracts and statements from third parties.

steps.name: Review KYC package and accredited investor status
steps.description: The chief compliance officer checks the client's legal capacity to appoint the model manager, the identity of the signers, the accredited investor category certified in the draft IMA and that the client's beneficiary reporting duties are confirmed. Missing or stale items go back to the client with a list.

error.defect_description: A signer or accredited investor category is recorded wrongly.

control.basis: OSC decision of 17 May 2017 on the model manager, paras 11 and 31(f): member certifies accredited investor status; the model manager KYC policy verifies identity, objectives and risk tolerance

evidence.note: Control content from the OSC decision; 25% incomplete rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Draft or revise the investment management agreement
steps.description: Investment counsel drafts the discretionary IMA from the model manager's standard form: services, interim permitted investments until the client's policy is set, pools and segregated mandates, reporting, cost recovery, termination and withdrawal terms, the misrepresentation and pool risk disclosures, and escalation of complaints. On later rounds counsel marks up the client's comments.

error.defect_description: A schedule conflicts with the client's statute or policy, found by client counsel or the board.

control.basis: The model manager Act, 2015 s. 9(1)2 requires an IMA with each member; OSC decision of 17 May 2017 requires termination, misrepresentation and risk disclosures in the IMA or subscription agreement

evidence.note: Required IMA content from the OSC decision; interim low-risk schedule from the judges' board report. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Client and its counsel review the IMA
steps.description: The client's staff and outside counsel review the draft against their statute, policy and fiduciary duties and return a mark-up, often on liability, termination notice, reporting and cost recovery terms. Each round waits on the client's lawyers and internal sign-offs.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Complex legal negotiation named as a common source of delay; round length and 40% repeat rate (about 1.7 rounds) are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the cost recovery schedule
steps.description: The director of financial planning estimates the client's first-year share of the model manager's costs, sets the allocation keys that will apply to its portfolio and pools, and writes the cost recovery schedule and invoicing terms for the IMA. The client's finance staff usually ask for a worked example.

error.defect_description: Allocation key or start date set wrongly, corrected at the first quarterly bill.

evidence.note: The model manager charges clients on a cost recovery basis only; schedule content and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Client board approves the IMA
steps.description: The client's staff take the final IMA, the cost estimate and the interim investment approach to their board or investment committee at its next scheduled meeting. The board approves, asks for changes or defers.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Client's own governance: IMA approved under the member's internal governance (OSC decision of 17 May 2017, para 10); pension administrators' duty of care under Pension Benefits Act s. 22

next.condition: approved, waiting for a designation regulation

evidence.note: Board approval required by member governance; infrequent board meetings named as a delay. Branch shares are author estimates (new body types often need a regulation, as in the 2023 selections).

steps.name: Wait for the regulation that makes the client eligible
steps.description: Where the client is not a Crown agency, university or municipality already eligible under the Act, it can only become a member once the government amends the regulation to prescribe it. The model manager's CEO office and legal track the amendment; signing waits until it is filed.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager Act, 2015 s. 9(1)3: qualifying bodies, with any other body to be prescribed by regulation (O. Reg. 212/17 as amended)

evidence.note: Membership categories and prescription by regulation summarised in the OSC decision; 2023 onboarding waited on regulatory changes. Remaining wait after board approval is an author estimate.

steps.name: Execute the IMA and admit the member
steps.description: The chief client officer checks that the board resolution, KYC approval and any regulation are in place, signs the IMA with the general counsel and has the client recorded as a member. The signed agreement is filed and sent to finance, compliance and operations.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager Act, 2015 s. 9(1)2 (IMA with each member) and the model manager signing authorities

evidence.note: IMA execution required; judges' board engaged the model manager effective 17 March 2020 once the IMA was agreed. Touch and wait are author estimates.

steps.name: Map the client's policy to pools and strategies
steps.description: A portfolio strategist translates the client's current policy, or the interim permitted investments, into the model manager pools, segregated mandates and money market holdings, notes holdings that cannot move (private fund interests needing general partner consent) and drafts the initial target positions and the hand-off to the full asset mix review.

error.defect_description: A legacy holding is mapped to a pool the client's policy does not permit, caught by compliance coding or the readiness review.

evidence.note: The model manager translates the strategic mix into its strategies; judges' plan held money market until policy approved. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review legacy managers and plan the transition
steps.description: The head of manager research reviews each legacy mandate and fund: keep, terminate or move in kind into a pool. For a large liquid portfolio the team asks a transition manager for a pre-trade cost and risk estimate comparing in-kind transfer with liquidation, and writes the transition plan with dates, notices and currency hedging.

error.defect_description: Plan underestimates a market or fund that cannot be transferred in kind, causing a residual position.

evidence.note: Cost comparison of in-specie transfer versus liquidation, pre-trade estimates and FX hedging described in the sources; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the custody account opening package
steps.description: The head of investment operations completes the custodian's account opening forms for the client's segregated account and pool unit account: legal agreements, tax forms, authorised signers, standing settlement instructions, market sub-accounts and reporting access, and gets the client's signatures, some of which must be wet-signed or notarised.

error.defect_description: Form incomplete or signer details inconsistent; custodian returns it.

control.basis: OSC decision of 17 May 2017, paras 31(i) and 32: custodian due diligence and NI 81-102 custodian qualifications before a custodian holds member assets

evidence.note: Account opening documents, wet signatures and notarisation from the State Street roundtable. Touch time and error rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Custodian opens accounts and market sub-accounts
steps.description: The custodian runs its own KYC, has each file checked by two teams and opens the client accounts, sub-accounts in each market and reporting access. Queries on missing forms come back to operations and add days.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: custodian returns the package with queries

evidence.note: Custodian describes long timelines, two-team review and KYC before release; 10 to 45 day wait and 15% return rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Set up the client in the unitholder register
steps.description: The pool unit pricing manager creates the client's unitholder accounts in each pool it will hold, records the subscription agreement, authorised signers and the call-back list for cash instructions, and links the register to the new custody accounts. A second person checks the standing data against the signed documents.

error.defect_description: Signer or bank detail keyed wrongly, caught by the second check or the readiness review.

control.basis: Maker-checker review of unitholder and payment standing data (The model manager operations policy; common practice)

evidence.note: No public description of the model manager's register set-up; dual control on standing data is common practice. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Code the client's restrictions in the compliance engine
steps.description: A compliance analyst turns the IMA's permitted investments, limits and prohibited holdings into pre-trade and post-trade rules for the client's account and its pool holdings, then runs them against the expected day-one positions to check for false alerts.

error.defect_description: A limit is coded with the wrong scope or threshold.

evidence.note: Restrictions in each IMA must be built into systems that prevent contraventions; coding time and error rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Approve the coded restrictions
steps.description: The chief compliance officer compares the coded rules with the IMA clause by clause, reviews the test results and approves the rule set, or sends it back with corrections.

error.defect_description: A coding error is approved and surfaces as a false or missed alert after go-live.

control.basis: OSC decision of 17 May 2017, para 31(e): prevent investments that contravene restrictions set out in the IMA

evidence.note: Control from the OSC decision; 18% correction rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Set up the portfolio in the book of record, performance and data systems
steps.description: The investment data manager, with a business systems analyst, creates the client portfolio hierarchy, accounts, benchmarks and asset class mapping in the book of record, the performance system and the warehouse, adds the custodian feeds and builds the client's monthly report template.

error.defect_description: Benchmark or account mapping wrong, found when the first report does not reconcile.

evidence.note: No public description; set-up steps follow the systems in the organisation file. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Set up accounting structure and close calendar
steps.description: The director of investment accounting sets up the client's ledger structure, fiscal year end, month-end close and valuation calendar, audit confirmation contacts and the fields fund accounting needs to produce day-one values.

error.defect_description: Fiscal year end or valuation calendar set wrongly.

evidence.note: Author estimate based on the fund accounting role in the organisation file.

steps.name: Hold the transition readiness review
steps.description: The chief client officer chairs a go or no-go meeting where operations, compliance, legal, data and accounting confirm their set-up is complete and tested and the transfer date still suits the client and the market. Open items either get fixed first or the date moves.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager onboarding governance: go or no-go sign-off before client assets move (common practice)

evidence.note: Readiness gates are common in multi-party transitions; 20% not-ready rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Client approves the transition plan and signs transfer directions
steps.description: The client's staff approve the transition plan and sign letters of direction to their current custodian and legacy managers to deliver securities and cash, terminate mandates on the agreed date and send final holdings files.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate; transfer directions must come from the asset owner.

steps.name: Legacy custodian and managers deliver the assets
steps.description: On the transfer date, usually a month end, the old custodian delivers securities free of payment and wires cash to the new accounts, and legacy pooled funds redeem or re-register units. In-kind transfers settle over several days and some markets lag.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Mix of in-specie transfers, redemptions and re-registrations in the case study; judges' plan cash moved six days after engagement. Wait range is an author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile received assets to legacy statements
steps.description: A reconciliation analyst compares every position, quantity, cost and cash balance received at the custodian with the legacy custodian's closing statement and the transition plan, loads the day-one book of record and sends any differences to the legacy custodian or manager.

error.defect_description: A small break is cleared without evidence and reappears at the first month end.

control.basis: Accurate books and records of member transactions (OSC decision of 17 May 2017, para 31(c)); reconciliation before positions are used

evidence.note: Books and records duty from the OSC decision; 40% break rate is an author estimate for a first-time transfer between custodians.

steps.name: Legacy custodian or manager resolves breaks
steps.description: The legacy custodian or manager answers the analyst's break list: missing securities still in transit, unsettled trades, income received after the transfer date or missing cost and tax lot data. Answers often take several chases.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate of response time from a former custodian.

steps.name: Instruct the initial pool subscriptions
steps.description: The pool unit pricing manager prepares the client's first subscriptions into each pool, in kind for transferred securities and in cash for the rest, at the agreed dealing date, and sends them for processing. Securities that stay segregated are left in the client account.

error.defect_description: Wrong pool or amount on an in-kind subscription, found in the unit confirmation.

control.basis: OSC decision of 17 May 2017: pool units distributed only to members that are accredited investors and whose IMA or subscription agreement contains the required disclosures

evidence.note: Condition on unit distributions from the OSC decision; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Oversee transition trading and review the post-trade report
steps.description: Where legacy assets are sold or rebalanced, the transition manager or the model manager's desk trades over several days; afterwards the head of manager research compares the post-trade report with the pre-trade estimate using implementation shortfall from the prior close and records the cost for the client report. Cash-only clients skip the trading but still wait for the first investment into pools.

error.defect_description: Cost measured against a favourable benchmark, understating the real cost.

control.basis: Transition cost reporting on the T-Standard implementation shortfall basis (T-Charter industry practice)

evidence.note: Case study: trading completed within six days and compared with the pre-trade estimate; T-Standard measures from the prior close. Review time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Draft the transition report
steps.description: The relationship manager writes the report to the client: assets received, positions moved in kind or sold, transition costs, day-one positions and values by pool and account, holdings that remain segregated and what happens next. Fund accounting supplies the values after the first close.

error.defect_description: A value or cost figure does not tie to accounting.

evidence.note: Post-transition report comparing results with estimates described in the case study; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review and release the transition report
steps.description: The director of client relationships ties the report's totals to the accounting values and the post-trade report, checks the wording and releases it to the client, or returns it for corrections.

error.defect_description: Error passes to the client.

control.basis: Client reporting review before release (The model manager client reporting practice)

evidence.note: Author estimate of review effort and correction rate.

steps.name: Hand over to steady-state service and close the project
steps.description: The relationship manager holds a close-out meeting with the client, confirms reporting and cash instruction contacts, hands the client to client service and portfolio construction for the full asset mix review, and records open items and lessons in the CRM.
outputs: client policy record for asset mix review

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate; meeting date depends on client availability.

exceptions.name: Client needs a designation regulation
exceptions.description: The client is not in an eligible category, so signing waits for the government to amend the regulation; in a few cases the amendment is not made in time and the client withdraws.

exceptions.name: IMA reopened by the client board
exceptions.description: The board asks for changes to liability, termination or cost terms, sending the agreement back to counsel and to the next board meeting.

exceptions.name: Custodian returns the account package
exceptions.description: Missing tax forms, unsigned or non-notarised documents or inconsistent signer data send the package back to operations.

exceptions.name: Day-one reconciliation breaks
exceptions.description: Securities in transit, unsettled legacy trades, late income or missing cost data mean positions do not agree with the legacy statement and must be chased.

exceptions.name: Legacy private fund interests cannot move
exceptions.description: Limited partnership interests need general partner consent to transfer, so they stay in a segregated client account managed by the asset manager and are excluded from the pool subscriptions.

exceptions.name: Cash-only client held in money market
exceptions.description: A client funded with cash and without an approved long-term policy is invested in money market instruments under an interim schedule until its asset mix is approved, as the judges' plan was from March 2020.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from selection to transition report
benchmarks.population: Public body clients of an Ontario public-sector asset manager

evidence.note: Not a measured distribution. One documented case: the guarantee fund was selected on 5 December 2023 and its assets were managed from 25 June 2024 (203 days); the policy mix was fully implemented on 1 January 2025 (393 days). A transition report follows the transfer by some weeks, so p50 is set at 230. State Street research cited by MJ Hudson found 70% of US transitions had 1 to 12 months of delay or implementation.

benchmarks.population: FSRA Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund, $1.2 billion, 2023-2024

evidence.note: 5 December 2023 to 25 June 2024.
25 June 2024 to 1 January 2025.

benchmarks.population: Provincial Judges Pension Board, $421 million in cash, March 2020

evidence.note: The model manager engaged effective 17 March 2020; funds transferred 23 March 2020 into money market instruments.

benchmarks.population: Multi-asset pension fund merger, nine legacy mandates, 2020

evidence.note: Trading started 19 February 2020 and was completed within six days of implementation.
Over 1,000 emails and weekly project calls.

pain_points.description: Legal negotiation of the IMA and the client's board calendar set the pace; each extra round of comments or a deferred board meeting adds weeks.

evidence.note: Infrequent trustee meetings and legal negotiation named as main sources of delay.

pain_points.description: New types of public body cannot sign until a regulation prescribes them, a step neither party controls.

evidence.note: Onboarding of the 2023 selections waited on regulatory changes and contracts.

pain_points.description: Custody account opening needs paper, notarised and wet-signed documents and is reviewed twice by the custodian; returned packages restart the clock.

evidence.note: Roundtable on account opening pain points.

pain_points.description: Assets can sit in cash or money market for months while the client's long-term policy is still being approved, an unmeasured opportunity cost.

evidence.note: Judges' plan held money market from March 2020 with its policy unfinished at March 2021; event shortfall measures the cost of delay.

pain_points.description: Many parties (client, two custodians, legacy managers, transition manager, internal teams) are coordinated by email and spreadsheets, and the process runs too rarely for staff to build routine.

evidence.note: 17 parties and over 1,000 emails in one transition.

assumptions: The process starts at selection and includes the IMA, because the organisation file lists the accepted proposal and regulation change as triggers; the proposal itself and the later full asset mix review are separate processes.

Work that runs in parallel after signing (policy mapping, transition planning, custody, register, compliance, data and accounting set-up) is listed in sequence with short waits and marked concurrent_with, so the simulated cycle time follows the longest chain, which is the custodian's account opening.
External steps carry zero touch time; client, custodian and government effort sits inside the waits, so hands-on time and cost cover the asset manager's staff only.

Branch shares (35% need a regulation, 9% board changes, 3% plus 5% withdrawals, 40% reconciliation breaks) are author estimates; the regulation share reflects that the 2023 selections were new body types.
Hands-on times are author estimates for a client with a few legacy mandates; a large pension plan with private holdings would take several times longer, and a cash-only client much less.

The cycle time benchmark rests on one documented case (the guarantee fund in 2023-2024) because the asset manager does not publish onboarding timelines; it is after the reference period but uses the same process.

compliance_analyst and reconciliation_analyst are organisation file roles that the process_map entry does not list; they are added because coding restrictions and reconciling day-one positions are analyst work.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges (Job Bank wages, 1.35 loading).
